
The State of Pernambuco publishes data for its analysts on an S3 object
store, `s3.pe.gov.br`. Each project has a bucket (`iaempe`,
`horizonte-fiscal`, ...) and a key pair that reads it, sometimes writes
it. `s3pe` is the client: nine verbs that move R objects and files in and
out, with every request signed, retried on transient failures and
verified against the server's checksum.

This vignette is not evaluated: the store needs credentials.

## Credentials

Put the key pair in `~/.Renviron` and restart R. `S3PE_BUCKET` is the
bucket used when you do not say which one.

```
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=GK...
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
S3PE_BUCKET=iaempe
```

`s3_config()` shows what the package resolved (the secret is never
printed). Every verb takes a `config` argument, so you can also build one
explicitly, for another endpoint or another key:

```{r}
library(s3pe)
s3_config()

cfg <- s3_config(bucket = "horizonte-fiscal",
                 access_key = Sys.getenv("HF_KEY"),
                 secret_key = Sys.getenv("HF_SECRET"))
```

Keys are either relative to the bucket or full `s3://bucket/key` URLs; the
URL wins.

## Reading

`read_s3()` chooses the reader by the key's extension:

```{r}
# JSON -> list
meta <- read_s3("dados/metadata.json")
meta$ultimo_mes

# gzipped CSV -> tibble (readr); `...` reaches the reader
icms <- read_s3("s3://horizonte-fiscal/series/estado/icms.csv.gz",
                col_types = "Dncl")

# GeoJSON -> sf, when sf is installed
municipios <- read_s3("dados/pe_municipios.geojson")

# Parquet -> data frame (nanoparquet)
painel <- read_s3("etl/painel_iaempe.parquet")

# anything else -> raw bytes; or ask for them
png <- read_s3("nota_tecnica/figura1.png")
txt <- read_s3("dados/metadata.json", format = "text")
```

The buckets of the platform upload a manifest last. If `metadata.json`
says the batch is 2026-08, every file of that batch is already there:
read it first and use it as the version of what you cache.

```{r}
cache <- "iaem-cache.rds"
meta <- read_s3("dados/metadata.json")
if (!file.exists(cache) || readRDS(cache)$ultimo_mes != meta$ultimo_mes) {
  batch <- list(
    ultimo_mes = meta$ultimo_mes,
    series = read_s3("dados/series.json"),
    ranking = read_s3("dados/ranking.json")
  )
  saveRDS(batch, cache)
}
```

## Writing

`write_s3()` is the reverse: the extension decides the format and the
content type. Use a prefix of your own (`dados/` belongs to the
automatic mirror, which may overwrite it).

```{r}
write_s3(painel, "nota_tecnica/painel.parquet")
write_s3(painel, "nota_tecnica/painel.csv.gz")
write_s3(list(gerado_em = Sys.time(), linhas = nrow(painel)),
         "nota_tecnica/manifest.json", pretty = TRUE)
write_s3(modelo, "nota_tecnica/modelo.rds")
write_s3(c("# Nota técnica", "", "Texto..."), "nota_tecnica/README.md")
```

Follow the platform's convention: upload the data first, the manifest
last.

## Files

`upload_s3()` and `download_s3()` move files without reading them into R.
A key ending in `/` gets the file's name appended; downloads are written
to a `.s3pe-part` file and renamed when complete and verified.

```{r}
upload_s3("output/figura1.png", "nota_tecnica/")
download_s3("dados/pe_municipios.geojson", "data/pe_municipios.geojson",
            overwrite = TRUE)
```

## The rest of the bucket

```{r}
list_s3("dados/")                     # tibble: key, size, last_modified, etag
head_s3("dados/metadata.json")        # one row, or NULL
exists_s3("dados/metadata.json")      # TRUE/FALSE
delete_s3("nota_tecnica/rascunho.csv")
buckets_s3()
```

## When things go wrong

Every failure is an error with a class, so a pipeline stops by default
and you can catch exactly what you expect:

```{r}
meta <- tryCatch(
  read_s3("dados/metadata.json"),
  s3pe_error_not_found = function(e) NULL
)
```

- `s3pe_error_config`: no credentials, no bucket, bad endpoint.
- `s3pe_error_not_found` (404), `s3pe_error_access` (403),
  `s3pe_error_http` (other statuses, with `$status` and `$code`).
- `s3pe_error_transport`: the server could not be reached, after three
  attempts with a 1 s and a 2 s pause.
- `s3pe_error_integrity`: the bytes that arrived are not the bytes that
  were sent.

Transfers print one line each (`↑ s3://iaempe/nota_tecnica/painel.parquet
(12.3 MB, 0.8 s)`); silence them with `options(s3pe.quiet = TRUE)` or
`S3PE_QUIET=1`.

## Inside the condepe server

The server that hosts the store talks to it on the loopback interface:

```{r}
options(s3pe.endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:9003")
```

## Other editions

The same verbs exist in Python (`pip install s3pe`), Rust
(`cargo install s3pe`, with the `s3pe` command line) and Go
(`go get github.com/StrategicProjects/s3pe`). They share one
specification and one test vector, so a key written by one is read by
the others.
